{{Quote|This holiday is yours, but we all share with you the hope that this day brings us closer to freedom, and to harmony, and to peace. No matter how different we appear, we're all the same in our struggle against the powers of evil and darkness. I hope that this day will always be a day of joy in which we can reconfirm our dedication and our courage. And more than anything else, our love for one another. This is the promise of the Tree of Life.|Princess Leia Organa|audio=LeiaLifeDay.flac|<ref name="SWHS" />}}
'''Life Day''' was a [[Wookiee/Legends|Wookiee]] holiday celebrated by the inhabitants of [[Kashyyyk/Legends|Kashyyyk]]. It was a celebration of the [[Planet/Legends|planet's]] diverse ecosystem and the many forms of life it encompassed. It was also a [[Time/Legends|time]] to remember family members who had [[Death/Legends|died]], and the young ones who continued to bring new life to a family. Life Day was a sacred holiday, and many Wookiees considered it their duty to return to Kashyyyk in order to celebrate it. Life Day was held once every three local [[Standard year/Legends|years]] for many generations, but it became celebrated more frequently as its popularity slowly grew to the wider [[The galaxy/Legends|galaxy]]. Despite its name, the holiday could also be celebrated over the course of at least a couple [[Standard day/Legends|days]]. By the time of the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], Life Day's importance to the Wookiees had become more pronounced. Because Wookiees were spread across the galaxy, either for personal reasons or due to their [[Slavery/Legends|enslavement]] to the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]], the holiday was celebrated as a way to remain in touch with their history. Outside of the traditional Wookiee holiday, the term "life day" or "lifeday" was sometimes used to describe the [[Birthday/Legends|anniversary]] of one's birth.

==History==
===Ancient history===
{{Quote|A big part of their Life Day celebration is a ''spiritual passage'' to the Life Tree&hellip; where Wookiee culture began! Orga root helps them make the journey!|Han Solo, to C-3PO|<ref name="TKD">"[[The Kashyyyk Depths]]"</ref>}}
[[File:AncientLifeDay.jpg|170px|thumb|''Ancient Life Day'' painting]]
The origins of Life Day lay in the culture of the [[Wookiee/Legends|Wookiees]],<ref name="CWABlog">{{WebCite|url=http://www.clonewarsadventures.com/news/detail.action?articleId=1126|text=Life Day Returns!|work=the official [[Star Wars: Clone Wars Adventures (video game)|''Clone Wars Adventures'']] website|archivedate=20111208024549|nolive=1}}</ref> [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]]<ref name="EGTAS">[[The Essential Guide to Alien Species (real-world book)|''The Essential Guide to Alien Species'']]</ref> [[Mammal/Legends|mammals]]<ref name="AE">''[[Alien Encounters]]''</ref> who hailed from the [[Tree/Legends|arboreal]] [[Planet/Legends|world]] of [[Kashyyyk/Legends|Kashyyyk]],<ref name="EGTAS" /> with evidence that Wookiees celebrated the holiday by beating [[Tree-drum music|tree drums]] as early as [[1,500,000 BBY]].<ref name="Slugthrowers" /> The [[Tree of Life/Legends|Tree of Life]] was the birthplace of Wookiee culture,<ref name="TKD" /> and it served as a central gathering place for the holiday.<ref name="SWHS" /> For many generations, Life Day was celebrated every three local [[Standard year/Legends|years]],<ref name="CSWE" /> but as the joyous holiday spread throughout [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]], many [[Species/Legends|species]] and cultures began holding the celebration once a year.<ref name="SOELifeDay" />

===During the Galactic War===
{{Quote|This disgraceful menace of a 'holiday,' during which time you are expected to comply fully with this edict, will last approximately two weeks on the Galactic Standard Calendar.|Extract from the Imperial Edict GR-1NC4|<ref name="Grinch">{{TORweb|url=info/news/blog/20131216|text=IMPERIAL EDICT GR-1NC4}}</ref>}}
[[File:Life_Day_revelers.png|thumb|A group of Life Day Revelers in 3640 BBY]]
By the end of the [[Cold War (Galactic Republic–Sith Empire)|Cold War]]<ref name="SWTOR">''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic]]''</ref> around [[3640 BBY]],<ref name="DateTOR">''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic Encyclopedia]]''</ref> the tradition of exchanging gifts and decorating homes with festive Life Day flair had already become a mainstream aspect of the holiday. By the [[Time/Legends|time]] of the [[Galactic War]], [[Hologram/Legends|holographic]] [[Life Day Holo-Tree|Life Day Trees]] could even be found on the [[Core Worlds/Legends|Core World]] of [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]], [[Capital/Legends|capital]] [[City/Legends|city]] of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]]. To celebrate Life Day, a jolly old man dubbed the "[[Master of Ceremonies]]" set up shop on the Republic's [[Carrick Station]], along with an entourage of [[Life Day Revelers]] comprising of [[Human/Legends|Humans]] and Wookiees. While the Republic welcomed the Master and his followers without issue,<ref name="SWTOR" /> [[Imperial Edict GR-1NC4]] heavily discouraged citizens of the [[Sith Empire (Post–Great Hyperspace War)|Sith Empire]] from participating in Life Day, largely because of certain activities being deemed unbecoming of Imperial citizenry. Regardless, the Master of Ceremonies had somehow obtained an official license to peddle his "holiday cheer" in the Galactic Trade Market sector of the Empire's [[Vaiken Spacedock]]<ref name="Grinch" /> in the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]],<ref name="SWTOR" /> an error for which those in licensing had been punished to the fullest extent of Imperial law. Despite this oversight, the sale of Life Day goods was allowed to proceed, however items sold by the Master of Ceremonies remained under review per [[Section 53-T]] of Imperial law, and citizens were warned that purchasing such items may constitute an official contraband violation. The edict also noted that the Revelers' presence coincided with the reappearance of the ''[[Gray Secant]]'', an ancient [[Gree (species)/Legends|Gree]] [[Starship/Legends|starship]], over the planet [[Ilum/Legends|Ilum]]&mdash;which marked the return of the once powerful [[Gree Enclave/Legends|Gree Enclave]] to known [[Realspace/Legends|space]].<ref name="Grinch" />
{{GameMechanics|legends=1|Star Wars: The Old Republic}}
At any rate, the anti-Life Day edict was widely ignored, and some Imperial citizens indulged in a number of tawdry activities, like [[Snowball (object)|snowball]] fights, launching [[Fireworks/Legends|fireworks]], and embracing other Wookiees in celebration.<ref name="SWTOR" />
{{Endgame}}

===During the Clone Wars===
{{Quote|Well done, General! I think we have won! Now we can return to the parties and fun!|Commander Cody, to a Jedi General, after defeating General Grievous on Life Day|audio=CWACodiLifeDay.flac|<ref name="CWAOrbUpdate">{{SonyForumsCite|url=cw/posts/list.m?topic_id=1877|text=Server Maintenance for December 17, 2010}}</ref>}}
[[Millennium/Legends|Thousands]] of years later,<ref name="NEC">''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''</ref> during the time of [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], Life Day was celebrated at the main [[Jedi Temple/Legends|Jedi Temple]] on Coruscant. The hallowed halls of the temple were decorated with garlands and [[Color/Legends|colored]] [[Life Day Orb/Legends|Life Day orbs]] hanging from the ceiling, along with a small [[Wroshyr tree/Legends|wroshyr tree]] surrounded by gift boxes in the temple's main hall.<ref name="CWA">{{TCWA|loc=Main Hall}} {{C|"Life Day" festival, 2010&ndash;2013}}</ref> [[Service droid/Legends|Service droids]], including the [[R2-series astromech droid/Legends|R2-series]] [[Astromech droid/Legends|astromech droids]] [[P3-NUT]]<ref name="Peanut">{{TCWA|set=P3-NUT}}</ref> and [[6R-0WL]],<ref name="Growl">{{TCWA|set=6R-0WL}}</ref> and the [[R5-series astromech droid]] [[BR-RR]], bore festive paintings.<ref name="Brrr">{{TCWA|set=BR-RR}}</ref> Some [[Clone trooper/Legends|clone troopers]] donned fancy [[Armor/Legends|armors]], such as [[Nutcracker Clone Trooper|nutcracker armor]]<ref name="Nutcracker">{{TCWA|set=Nutcracker Clone Trooper}}</ref> and [[Life Day clone trooper armor]].<ref name="LifeDayClone">{{TCWA|set=Life Day Clone Trooper}}</ref> Even the [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]] was known to wear festive [[Clothing/Legends|clothing]] during the holiday.<ref name="ObiWan">{{TCWA|set=Festive Obi-Wan Kenobi}}</ref> While the Republic was quite fond of Life Day, the opposing [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]] were not, as evidenced by their offensive attack on a settlement on the [[Water/Legends|icy]] planet of [[Orto Plutonia/Legends|Orto Plutonia]] that celebrated the occasion. Like the Jedi Temple on Coruscant, the Orto Plutonian settlement was decorated with garlands and Life Day orbs. A number of wroshyr trees had also been placed throughout the settlement, surrounded by numerous gift boxes. The [[Pantoran/Legends|Pantorans]], hoping to mend their past rifts with the native [[Talz/Legends|Talz]], sought to deliver these gifts to them as a token of goodwill. The infamous [[Separatist Droid Army/Legends|Separatist Droid Army]] [[Supreme Commander of the Droid Armies/Legends|Supreme Commander]], [[General/Legends|General]] [[Grievous/Legends|Grievous]], schemed to put a stop to this by sending [[Gender/Legends|his]] [[Battle droid/Legends|battle droids]] to attack the settlement and steal all the presents.<ref name="CWAGrievous">{{TCWA|Grievous Steals Life Day}} {{C|"Life Day" festival, 2010&ndash;2013}}</ref>
{{GameMechanics|legends=1|Star Wars: Clone Wars Adventures (video game)|''Star Wars: Clone Wars Adventures'' video game}}
However, under the leadership of [[Clone Marshal Commander/Legends|Clone Commander]] [[Cody/Legends|Cody]] and a [[Jedi General/Legends|Jedi General]], the [[Grand Army of the Republic/Legends|Grand Army of the Republic]] and the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]] stood poised to drive Grievous and the other Separatists off. Shortly after Grievous landed on Orto Plutonia aboard his [[Belbullab-22 starfighter/Legends|Belbullab-22 starfighter]], the [[Soulless One/Legends|''Soulless One'']], a large [[Droid/Legends|droid]] [[Army/Legends|army]] consisting of [[B1-series battle droid/Legends|B1-Series battle droids]], [[B2-series super battle droid/Legends|B2 super battle droids]], [[DSD1 dwarf spider droid/Legends|DSD1 dwarf spider droids]], [[Armored Assault Tank/Legends|Armored Assault Tanks]], [[NR-N99 Persuader-class droid enforcer/Legends|NR-N99 ''Persuader''-class droid enforcers]], and [[Single Trooper Aerial Platform/Legends|Single Trooper Aerial Platforms]] invaded the settlement. Despite a relentless onslaught of five waves of battle droids, which included even General Grievous himself, the assortment of defensive fixtures constructed throughout the settlement managed to pick away at the attackers. In the end, when Grievous realized all was lost, he called for a retreat, and hastily ran away from the battlefield.<ref name="CWAGrievous" />
{{Endgame}}

===During the Galactic Civil War===
{{Quote|Bah, humbug!|Emperor Palpatine on Life Day|<ref name="SWG Sony News">{{SonyCite|url=players/news_archive.vm?id=68147&month=122008|text=Friday Feature &ndash; ''Corellia Times'' Exclusive: Life Day Revealed}}</ref>}}
[[File:LifeDay.png|thumb|A wroshyr tree donated to Queen Kylantha by Wookiee elders for a Life Day celebration following 0 BBY]]
By the time of the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], Life Day had become increasingly important to the Wookiees since the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] had [[Slavery/Legends|enslaved]] many of their kind.<ref name="Holiday">{{SonyCite|url=content.jsp?page=Happy%20Holidays%202003|text=Happy Holidays 2003}}</ref> One particular Life Day holiday was celebrated around [[3 BBY/Legends|3 BBY]],<ref name="Dawn">{{SWBoards|url=thread.jspa?threadID=152583&start=870#15782460|thread=Holocron continuity database questions|user=[[Leland Chee|Tasty Taste]]|date=2006-10-13|time=8:50 AM|quote=I've got ''RD'' at 2 BBY}}</ref><ref name="DawnExplaine">According to [[Holocron continuity database]] manager [[Leland Chee]], ''[[Rebel Dawn]]'' took place in [[2 BBY/Legends|2 BBY]]. The book indicates that the most recent Life Day occurred "about a [[Standard year/Legends|standard year]]" ago. This article's date is therefore derived from simple math based on this reference explanation.</ref> while other various festivities were carried out between [[0 BBY/Legends|0 BBY]] and [[3 ABY/Legends|3 ABY]],<ref name="SWGDate">According to its [[opening crawl]], ''[[Star Wars Galaxies]]'' was set sometime after [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''Star Wars'': Episode IV ''A New Hope'']]. One character in the [[Star Wars video games|game]], [[Ruwan Tokai]], referenced the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|destruction]] of the [[DS-1 Orbital Battle Station/Legends|Death Star]] as occurring one [[Standard year/Legends|year]] earlier, placing the timeline somewhere around [[1 ABY/Legends|1 ABY]]. However, the existence of other characters and quests in the game indicated a timeline of anywhere from [[0 ABY/Legends|0]] to [[3 ABY/Legends|3 ABY]].</ref> including one noteworthy celebration halfway through the year [[1 ABY/Legends|1 ABY]],<ref name="Leland">{{SWBoards|url=thread.jspa?threadID=152583&start=870#15778940|thread=Holocron continuity database questions|user=[[Leland Chee|Tasty Taste]]|date=2006-10-12|time=6:13 PM|quote=Wookiee Life Day occurs every 3 years, one of which fell at ~1.5 ABY. There might be non-Wookiee cultures which call birthdays life days. Galaxies celebrated Life Day in "real time" at around Christmas.}}</ref> in which the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]] [[Heroes of Yavin/Legends|hero]] [[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]] attempted to bring his Wookiee companion [[Chewbacca/Legends|Chewbacca]] [[Homeworld|home]] to Kashyyyk in time to see his [[Chewbacca's family|family]]. Despite being forced to evade an Imperial [[Blockade of Kashyyyk (1 ABY)|blockade of Kashyyyk]], Han successfully brought Chewie to his [[Chewbacca's home|home]] in [[Rwookrrorro/Legends|Rwookrrorro]]. They also made it in time to partake in the Tree of Life ceremony, as did [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]] and his two [[Droid/Legends|droids]], [[R2-D2/Legends|R2-D2]] and [[C-3PO/Legends|C-3PO]]. [[Princess/Legends|Princess]] [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia Organa]] was also there to sing "[[A Day to Celebrate]]," a celebratory Life Day hymn. The ceremony also saw the inclusion of many other Wookiees, all of whom wore ceremonial [[Life Day robes/Legends|Life Day robes]].<ref name="SWHS" /> This was not the only time Han Solo and Chewbacca traveled to Kashyyyk for Life Day. During a subsequent holiday, the duo arrived to the planet along with R2-D2 and C-3PO, only to discover that the [[Wookiee Chieftain|Wookiee elder]] had cancelled the event due to a lack of [[Orga/Legends|Orga]] root. Chewbacca, angered by this decision, attacked the elder. Han Solo defused the situation by agreeing to travel to Kashyyyk's lower levels to search for the root. Journeying with Chewbacca and the droids, the group managed to acquire the root, after witnessing the [[Plant/Legends|plants]] [[Death/Legends|killing]] a group of Imperials. An Imperial [[Scientist/Legends|scientist]] named [[Gyla Petro]] was spared, however, and she joined the group during the Tree of Life ceremony.<ref name="TKD" />

During the days leading up to one particular Life Day, a scurrilous [[Smuggler/Legends|smuggler]] by the name of [["Shady" Pers]] stole all of the Orga root on Kashyyyk. In order to save the holiday, a Wookiee by the name of [[Tebeurra]] traveled off-world to find help. Accompanied by a protocol droid, and donning a long, red Life Day robe, Tebuerra talked with various people at the local [[Spaceport/Legends|spaceport]].<ref name="TCG">{{SWGTCG|set=Champions of the Force|scenario=Happy Life Day promotional scenario}}</ref>
{{GameMechanics|legends=1|Champions of the Force (SWGTCG)|''Champions of the Force''}}
Curiosity got the better of one [[Spacer/Legends|spacer]], who approached Tebeurra to see what she was looking for. Communicating in native [[Shyriiwook/Legends|Shyriiwook]] through the translation capabilities of her protocol droid, Tebeurra explained to the spacer that the stolen Orga root needed to be recovered from "Shady" Pers before the Life Day holiday could commence. She furthermore explained the importance of Orga root, as eating the root helped them complete the spiritual passage to the Tree of Life. The spacer dismissed the details, but agreed to help the distressed Wookiee. Just a few days later, the spacer monitored the warehouse where "Shady" Pers stored all his shipments. Breaking into a rear entrance, the spacer hoped to sneak in and recover all the boxes one at a time. Before they could grab the first crate, the spacer heard the metallic voice of a [[Battle droid/Legends|battle droid]] sounding an intruder alert. The droid began firing its [[Blaster/Legends|blaster]] at the spacer, ruining their infiltration plans. As the spacer began to defend themselves, a loud voice rang throughout the facility. It was "Shady" Pers, announcing over the [[Speaker/Legends|loudspeaker]] that the spacer would never be able to get past his [[Guard droid/Legends|guard droids]]. He urged the individual to surrender, but the spacer knew that was not a viable option. The only option was was to defeat his droid guards, and rescue the Orga root through sheer force. Each crate was guarded by one droid, forcing the spacer to defeat them all in order to recover the plants. The spacer ultimately succeeded in doing so, thus allowing the Life Day festivities to carry out unfettered.<ref name="TCG" />
{{Endgame}}

Also following the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]],<ref name="SWG" /> a member of Tebeurra's family named [[Kkatamik]] traveled to [[Vreni Island]] on Corellia, [[Varykino/Legends|Varykino]] on [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]], and [[Anchorhead/Legends|Anchorhead]] on [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]] to help spread word of the holiday.<ref name="SOELifeDay" /> Kkatamik sought to encourage travelers to visit his family so that they could learn more about Life Day. Aside from Tebeurra, Kkatamik's family also included the likes of [[Oraalarri]] the Elder, [[Anarra]], and [[Radrrl]]. The family was often forced to move around in order to escape persecution from the Empire. Regardless, during the Life Day festivities of that year, Kkatamik's family welcomed all individuals, regardless of their [[Politics/Legends|political]] beliefs. For Life Day, Oraalarri the Elder and his family of Wookiees traveled to the [[Forest/Legends|Forest]] [[Moon/Legends|Moon]] of [[Endor/Legends|Endor]], [[Yavin 4/Legends|Yavin 4]], and [[Dathomir/Legends|Dathomir]]. On each of those worlds, they set up camp, and prepared to receive a number of Life Day pilgrims referred to them by Kkatamik, including even those loyal to the Empire. Although they were wary of Imperials, and urged them to reconsider their allegiance, they still welcomed the opportunity to teach them about their sacred holiday traditions. The family also offered a number of gifts, including Life Day orbs and [[Painting/Legends|paintings]], such as those depicting [[Life Day Kashyyyk|Kashyyyk]], a [[Life Day Matriarch|matriarch]], and a [[Life Day Patriarch|patriarch]]. The family also offered red Life Day [[Robe/Legends|robes]] to their fellow Wookiee cousins.<ref name="SWG" />

During the 411th day of his [[Prison/Legends|imprisonment]] at the [[Kessel prison|Imperial Correctional Facility]] on [[Kessel/Legends|Kessel]], the Wookiee [[Gyylghrard]] helped a work gang of young Wookiees organize a secret Life Day celebration. They all agreed on the mid-day meal break as the safest and most logical time to hold the celebration, during which time [[Prisoner/Legends|prisoners]] went in shifts to eat [[Foodstuff/Legends|food]] wafers in the dim blue light of the meal hall. With the help of a [[Jawa/Legends|Jawa]] trustee who oversaw food storage, "Big Gyyl," as he was called by the children, found certain supplies. The quiet celebration began as soon as the slaves had settled in to eat. Lacking traditional Wookiee cuisine, they had to make do with the slave's food stores, which included a [[Ration pack/Legends|ration packet]] containing rehydrated [[Corellian/Legends|Corellian]] [[Ryshcate/Legends|ryshcate]] [[Cake/Legends|cake]]. Tucked beneath each piece of [[Bread/Legends|sweetbread]] was also a small [[Candle/Legends|candle]] and a simple, one-use [[sparkstick]]. After devouring their cakes, the lead female of the Wookiee gang softly growled the melody to the traditional hymn "A Day to Celebrate." The others soon joined in, and at the end of the song, the children would ignite their candles and let them burn for a single [[Standard minute/Legends|minute]]. The group begun the second iteration of the chorus, and on the word "dream," hundreds of sparksticks snapped in unison. This seemingly harmless act overloaded their electronic shackles, causing hundreds of chains to clank to the floor. In unison, the young slaves went berserk, and the rest joined in after a few [[Standard second|seconds]]. To suppress the situation, the mess hall's compliment of ten [[Stormtrooper/Legends|stormtroopers]] leveled their blasters at the kids. In the end, the mob of young prisoners attempted to escape, and fought all the way to the [[Hangar/Legends|launch bay]] before stormtroopers reportedly brought them down in a hail of recharged blaster fire. [[Warden/Legends|Warden]] [[Commander/Legends|Commander]] [[Dewt Kluskine]] had ordered the stormtroopers to shoot to kill. Gyylghrard, left injured during the [[Life Day massacre]], vowed revenge for the warden's murderous act.<ref name="Hope">{{Wizards|url=default.asp?x=starwars/article/sw20030515kessel3|series=Kessel: Hell in Space|text=Part 3: Hope in Darkness}}</ref>

Despite being under Imperial occupation, the major Kashyyykian city of [[Kachirho/Legends|Kachirho]] hosted at least one major Life Day celebration following the Battle of [[Yavin Prime/Legends|Yavin]].<ref name="ROTW">''[[Star Wars Galaxies: Rage of the Wookiees]]''</ref> This celebration was held concurrently to other festivities in [[Theed/Legends|Theed]] and [[Coronet City/Legends|Coronet]], capital cities of Naboo and Corellia respectively.<ref name="SWG" /> Under the watchful [[Eye/Legends|eye]] of the Empire, Wookiee elders had also granted [[Monarch of Naboo/Legends|Queen]] [[Kylantha]] and the city of Theed a Tree of Life as a gesture of goodwill.<ref name="Celebrate">{{SonyCite|url=players/news_archive.vm?id=67531&month=122007|text=Friday Feature &ndash; Celebrating Life Day}}</ref> The time-honored wroshyr trees could also be found in Kachirho and Coronet. Under the branches of these trees, the [[Bith/Legends|Bith]] [[Figrin D'an/Legends|Figrin D'an]] and his [[Band/Legends|band]] the [[Figrin D'an and the Modal Nodes/Legends|Modal Nodes]] played [[Music/Legends|music]]. Figrin D'an and his band made it a regular tradition to go on tour during the Life Day festivities held during the Galactic Civil War. Later on, [[Doaba Guerfel/Legends|Doaba Guerfel]] played host to Life Day, as did [[Dearic/Legends|Dearic]] on the [[Double Worlds|Double World]] of [[Talus/Legends|Talus]], and the town of [[Wayfar/Legends|Wayfar]] on Tatooine. At each of these cities, the band played their distinctive brand of festive music under the festively decorated wroshyr trees set up for the occasion.<ref name="SWG" /> The Human [[Saun Dann]] had a jovial spirit for the holiday, and aside from having looked over Chewbacca's family during the Life Day festivities<ref name="SWHS" /> of 1 ABY,<ref name="Leland" /> he also participated in the festivities held at the three aforementioned cities.<ref name="SWG" /> As a trader who sold goods back at his [[Trading post Wookiee Planet C|trading post]] on Kashyyyk,<ref name="SWHS" /> Saun Dann used Life Day as an opportunity to sell his festive wares in other parts of the galaxy, including soothing mugs of [[Hoth chocolate]], [[Wookiee-ookiee]]s, and holiday firework packages. Saun Dann had also ordered two cases of [[Life Day candy]] from the Naboo city of [[Keren/Legends|Keren]] to give to poor children. To his dismay, however, his shipment became delayed, and he worried something may have happened to it.<ref name="SWG" />
{{GameMechanics|legends=1|Star Wars Galaxies}}
To learn more, Saun Dann sent a spacer to meet with the [[Keren Shipping Master]] on Naboo. After an extensive investigation, which led to the [[Jawa mountain fortress/Legends|Jawa Mountain Fortress]] on Tatooine, and then the nearby city of [[Mos Espa/Legends|Mos Espa]], it was discovered that a slovenly Imperial stormtrooper named [[TK-555]] stole the [[Candy/Legends|candy]]. The spacer confronted the stormtrooper in the [[Mos Espa Podracer Cantina|Mos Espa cantina]], and although he was apologetic, and reluctantly agreed to donate 10,000 [[Galactic Credit Standard/Legends|credits]] to the [[Mos Espa orphanage]] as reparations, the candy had already been eaten. Because the spacer threatened to report him to his superiors, the stormtrooper convinced a local [[Toydarian/Legends|Toydarian]] [[Junk dealer/Legends|junk dealer]] by the name of [[Watto/Legends|Watto]] to sell a discounted [[Single Trooper Aerial Platform/Legends|Single Troop Aerial Platform]] to the spacer in exchange for their silence. In light of this situation, Dann looked for another gift to provide to the children out of his own supplies. Unfortunately for Dann, this would not be his last time as a victim of theft. During at least one other subsequent Life Day celebration, another shipment of the candy ended up falling into the [[Limb/Legends|hands]] of the same gluttonous stormtrooper.<ref name="SWG" />

By now, the Rebel Alliance had embraced Life Day as an opportunity to promote anti-Imperial sentiment through the use of [[Propaganda/Legends|propaganda]].<ref name="Revealed">{{SonyCite|url=players/news_archive.vm?id=68147&month=122008|text=Friday Feature &ndash; ''Corellia Times'' Exclusive: Life Day Revealed}}</ref> Under the direction of Wookiee freedom fighter [[Oolovv]], Rebel supporters were tasked with the responsibility of decorating trees throughout the cities of Dearic, Doaba Guerfel, and Wayfar as a visible show of support to the local populaces. The Rebels also took it upon themselves to provide piles of gifts to the poor. Imperial [[Spy/Legends|spies]], suspicious of this Rebel initiative, concluded that their efforts were actually a cover to [[Smuggler/Legends|smuggle]] weapons and Rebel propaganda in the gift boxes. In light of this questionable intelligence, the [[Trandoshan/Legends|Trandoshan]] trader [[Sstrigge]], working at the behest of the Empire, recruited loyal citizens to smash piles of presents spread throughout the streets of these three cities. Sstrigge encouraged the more zealous citizens to show off their allegiance to the Empire whilst destroying the alleged contraband. Confrontations between the Rebel merrymakers and Imperial saboteurs at times escalated into acts of public violence. However, the festivities at the three main target cities continued unfazed.<ref name="SWG" />
{{Endgame}}
[[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]], leader of the Empire, refused to acknowledge the efforts made by the Rebel Alliance during Life Day. And while [[Hol't Deb Orah]] of the ''[[Corellia Times|Corellian Times]]'' could not reach him for comment, Palpatine's publicist revealed that the [[Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] harbored disgust for the holiday, which he considered "humbug."<ref name="Revealed" />

==Traditions==
===Core tenets===
{{Quote|The Life Day orb is a traditional part of our celebration. It shows a field of stars representing the afterlife. We beings of Kashyyyk believe that when we die that we walk off into the stars.|translated=1|Tebeurra|<ref name="SWG" />}}
[[File:LifeDay-MOTESB.png|thumb|left|200px|Chewbacca celebrates Life Day with his honor family]]
In its deepest meaning, Life Day was a celebration of Kashyyyk's diverse ecosystem and the many forms of life it encompassed. It was also a time to remember family members who had died, and the young ones who continued to bring new life to a family.<ref name="CSWE" /> Wookiees greatly valued morality, courage, compassion and loyalty. A sacred and ancient Wookiee tradition was that of the [[Wookiee honor family|honor family]], which comprised of a Wookiee's closest friends and companions. These family members pledged a commitment to lay down their lives for one another,<ref name="SOELifeDay" /> a concept known as a [[Life debt/Legends|life debt]].<ref name="AGTSWU2">''[[A Guide to the Star Wars Universe, Second Edition, Revised and Expanded]]''</ref> These extended Wookiee families would customarily gather to celebrate a day of joy and harmony, as promised by the Tree of Life.<ref name="CSWE" /> Wookiees would often brave adverse conditions to make it home for the holiday, as it was an important time for family bonding and thankfulness. However, it was at times impossible or impractical for Wookiees to make the journey home. Despite being traditionally celebrated on Kashyyyk, and usually at the Tree of Life, the enslavement of Wookiees under the reign of the Galactic Empire oftentimes forced the species to hold their holiday wherever they were.<ref name="SOELifeDay" /> Life Day orbs, a Wookiee artifact, were a traditional symbol carried by Wookiees during the Life Day celebrations. The [[Glass/Legends|glass-like]], shining orbs constituted one of the holiday's most ancient of traditions, as evidenced by its portrayal in a painting titled ''[[Ancient Life Day]]'', in which it was seen being carried like a [[Lantern/Legends|lantern]]. The orbs typically contained a field of [[Star/Legends|stars]] representing the [[Netherworld of the Force/Legends|afterlife]]. The beings of Kashyyyk believed that when when they died, they would walk off into the stars.<ref name="SWG" /> The globes had a variety of uses during Life Day festivities; small ones were colored and attached to the branches of [[Life Day tree/Legends|ornamented trees]],<ref name="CWA" /> others were kept as memorabilia.<ref name="SWG" /> Most importantly, Wookiee households displayed such orbs on their tables and gathered around them before joining a silent [[Prayer/Legends|prayer]] ceremony.<ref name="SWHS" /> Over time, the tradition of putting up colorful decorations, like Life Day orbs,<ref name="CWABlog" /> [[Life Day Ornament|ornaments]], buntings, and [[Life Day Wreath|wreaths]],<ref name="SWG" /> had spread to other parts of the galaxy.<ref name="CWABlog" /> For many generations, Life Day was celebrated every three local years,<ref name="CSWE" /> but as the holiday became more popular, other cultures began holding the celebration once a year.<ref name="SOELifeDay" /> Despite its name, Life Day festivities could be celebrated over the course of several days. During the Galactic War, festivities were conducted over the course of approximately two [[Standard week/Legends|weeks]],<ref name="Grinch" /> whereas during the Galactic Civil War, festivities could be conducted over the course of at least a couple days.<ref name="TwoDays">Two characters in ''[[Star Wars Galaxies]]'', named [[Oolovv]] and [[Sstrigge]], would tell players to return "tomorrow" for additional Life Day activities, which suggests that Life Day festivities during the [[Time/Legends|time]] of the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]] could be carried out over the course of at least a couple [[Standard day/Legends|days]].</ref>

===Festive wear===
{{Quote|Since you are one of our own, you have a choice. You may choose a traditional Life Day robe that may only be worn by Wookiees or you may receive another gift.|translated=1|Oraalarri the Elder, to a fellow Wookiee|<ref name="SWG" />}}
[[File:WookieeLifeDayRobe-SWG.jpg|thumb|Wookiees often wore robes during Life Day.]]
Another ancient tradition<ref name="SWG" /> was that of the Life Day robe, red garments worn during the ceremonies.<ref name="SWHS" /> Although they were only intended to be worn by Wookiees,<ref name="SWG" /> the robes were at times appropriated by by other species.<ref name="Robes">{{TCWA|set=Life Day Robes}}</ref> However, Life Day robes were not the only type of clothing worn during the celebrations. [[Life Day Jacket]]s and [[Holiday Jacket]]s were warm, festive [[Jacket/Legends|jackets]] worn in celebration of the holiday. [[Kashyyyk Elite Hunter Bandolier]]s were also available during Life Day, a type of [[Bandolier/Legends|bandolier]] usually worn by the most prominent Wookiee [[Hunting/Legends|hunters]] of Kashyyyk.<ref name="SWG" /> During the [[Cloning/Legends|Clone]] Wars, Obi-Wan Kenobi wore a distinctive white and red robe, black [[Boot/Legends|boots]], white [[Glove/Legends|gloves]], and a large black [[Belt/Legends|belt]] with a [[Brass/Legends|brass-colored]] buckle. Complimenting his look was a drooping, festive [[Hat/Legends|hat]], white and red in color, and conical in appearance. Obi-Wan's choice of festive clothing was available to other Republic citizens during the holiday.<ref name="ObiWan" /> Even clone troopers wore celebratory suits of armor during the holiday, such as the colorful Nutcracker Clone Troopers<ref name="Nutcracker" /> and brightly lit Life Day Clone Troopers.<ref name="LifeDayClone" /> Figrin D'an and the Modal Nodes donned festive wear during Life Day, including long red holiday jackets, and Wookiee Life Day [[Merchant/Legends|vendors]] wore red and white [[Chef/Legends|chef's]] aprons. [[Wookiee Life Day Necklace]]s were a type of [[Necklace/Legends|necklace]] worn in honor of the holiday.<ref name="SWG" /> On the other hand, astromech droids,<ref name="SnowMaker">{{TCWA|set=Astromech Life Day Parts}}</ref> [[Protocol droid/Legends|protocol droids]]<ref name="Protocol">{{TCWA|set=Protocol Droid Life Day Parts}}</ref> and [[MSE-series]] droids could also be donned with an overlay of festive lights. Mouse droids could also be affixed with a wind-key and tail, to give it the appearance of a toy [[Mouse/Legends|mouse]].<ref name="Mouse">{{TCWA|set=Mouse Droid Life Day Parts}}</ref>

===Mainstream appeal===
{{Quote|I want to wish you a happy Wookiee Life Day!|Watto|audio=Watto-lifeday-01.flac|<ref name="SWG" />}}
Wookiees had a primitive patriarchy with a complicated lineage structure, initiation rites, and a religion that rejected materialism. However, as the holiday spread throughout the galaxy to other species and cultures,<ref name="SOELifeDay" /> the holiday took on a greater focus on consumerism,<ref name="ActionTidings">{{Wizards|url=default.asp?x=starwars/article/sw20041028bespin5|series=Bespin: Action Tidings|text=Part 5: An Exclusive!}}</ref> which included the purchase and exchange of gifts.<ref name="SWG" /> By the end of the Cold War, the so-called Master of Ceremonies would bestow a number of extravagant vehicles and other goods to citizens in exchange for gift parcels. The mysterious [[Gree technology|Gree]] [[Gree technology|Cyan Sphere]] was one such [[Speeder/Legends|speeder]]. Others had more of a Life Day-themed appearance, like the [[Sleigh I]], a [[Speeder bike/Legends|speeder bike]] which would jingle as it traveled across the ground. The [[Czerka Arms/Legends|Czerka Corporation]] had also produced the [[LD-1 Celebrator]], yet another [[Hoverbike/Legends|hoverbike]] which was decked with bright, festive [[Lamp/Legends|lights]]. The [[Podracer/Legends|Podracer-like]] [[Vectron]] [[J0-1Y]] and the [[Snowstorm Assault Speeder]] were additional festively-themed [[Repulsorcraft/Legends|repulsorcraft]] vehicles, the latter of which was armed with a [[Cannon/Legends|cannon]] capable of firing snowballs. In fact, the act of throwing snowballs at bystanders became something of a popular Life Day tradition itself. [[Life Day snowball bomb]]s were a specific type of snowball which celebrants would throw at one another. Despite their name, snowball [[Bomb/Legends|bombs]] were in fact completely harmless. Around the Coruscant [[Senate Building/Legends|Senate Building]], [[Dromund Kaas/Legends|Dromund Kaas]] [[Kaas City|city]] [[Monument to Lord Ergast]], and [[Nar Shaddaa/Legends|Nar Shaddaa]] [[Promenade]], a number of [[Hollis-series steward droid]]s were used as targets by celebrants during snowball fights.<ref name="SWTOR" /> At times, the Life Day snowball bombs contained miniature parcels, which could be used as a form of currency in exchange for other gifts.<ref name="Grinch" /> [[Life Day snowball cannon]]s were toy weapons which could also be utilized in a similar fashion on unsuspecting targets, covering them with a layer of gleaming snowflakes. [[Life Day Tinsel Bomb]]s were another harmless toy, which when thrown at others, would explode in a shower of colorful glitter.<ref name="SWTOR" /> The launching of fireworks became yet another holiday tradition.<ref name="SWG" /> Some fireworks, when ignited, produced patterns resembling Life Day Trees.<ref name="Grinch" /> Burning candles ritualistically was also another component of the holiday.<ref name="SWHS" />

Despite having originated on Kashyyyk,<ref name="CWABlog" /> a tropical world,<ref name="DB">{{DB|location|kashyyyk|Kashyyyk}}</ref> snow and other [[Winter/Legends|winter-like]] elements became a symbolic aspect of the holiday. For instance, the Life Day festivities in Dearic and Doaba Guerfel were conducted during times of considerable snowfall.<ref name="SWG" /> Despite its hot and arid climate,<ref name="SECR">''[[Star Wars Roleplaying Game Saga Edition Core Rulebook]]''</ref> even the town of Wayfar was subject to snowfall during its Life Day festivities, whether through natural or artificial means.<ref name="SWG" /> Indeed, [[Life Day Snowblower|snowblowers]] were a type of machine, which when placed in homes, would blow snow to create a frost-filled Life Day experience. [[Life Day Wall Freezer Unit|Wall freezer units]] were similarly used to create winter-like conditions in an abode.<ref name="Stronghold">''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic: Galactic Strongholds]]''</ref> [[Snow maker]]s were also affixed to astromech droids by the time of the Clone Wars, allowing them to emanate a shower of snow as they traveled about.<ref name="SnowMaker" /> Stalactite and icicle ceiling lights, icicle mounds, and [[wampa-skin rug]]s also made for fashionable Life Day decor.<ref name="Stronghold" /> Indeed, creatures like [[Wampa/Legends|wampas]] and [[Tauntaun/Legends|tauntauns]] became emblematic symbols of the holiday.<ref name="SWTOR" /> Despite being used as [[Carpet/Legends|rugs]],<ref name="Stronghold" /> wampas and their cubs became cherished pets during Life Day.<ref name="SWTOR" /> [[Wampa suit]] costumes were also made available.<ref name="Wampa">{{TCWA|set=Wampa Suit}}</ref> On the other hand, tauntaun mounts were sometimes affixed with glowing red [[Nose/Legends|noses]], antlers, and dressed festively for the occasion, all the way from the end of the Cold War<ref name="SWTOR" /> to the days of the Clone Wars.<ref name="Tauntaun">{{TCWA|set=Festive Tauntaun}}</ref> [[Icetromper/Legends|Icetromper]] mounts were also dressed with festive lights, and decked with bags of Life Day gift boxes.<ref name="SWTOR" /> [[Kowakian monkey-lizard/Legends|Kowakian monkey-lizards]] were available as Life Day pets, and dressed up in miniature boots and gloves, and [[bow-tie]]s colored in either green or red.<ref name="SWG" /> Droids made for acceptable Life Day companions as well. [[Copero/Legends|Copero]] [[Copero Jubilee Miniprobe|Jubilee Miniprobes]] were a type of [[Probe droid/Legends|probe droid]], affixed with kites, that were sold on Life Day during the time of the Old Republic.<ref name="SWTOR" /> Gathering around the [[fireplace]] was evidently another tradition, as [[Life Day Fireplace]]s,<ref name="Stronghold" /> [[Kashyyykian fireplace]]s, and rustic fireplaces were fixtures available for use during the holiday. In addition, [[Life Day Incense Burner]]s were a specific type of [[Incense/Legends|incense]] [[Incense burner/Legends|device]] suited for the ocassion. Indeed, many other pieces of furniture were centered around the holiday, like [[Life Day Lamp]]s, [[Wookiee Home Banner Kit]]s,<ref name="SWG" /> [[Life Day Pedestal]]s, potted trees, and [[snowglobe]]s. Some Life Day snowglobes depicted elements from various worlds, like [[Umbara/Legends|Umbara]], [[Ossus/Legends|Ossus]], [[Nathema]], and [[Copero/Legends|Copero]]. Others contained a variety of different droid ecosamples. The [[Model Umbaran Train]] was a type of model [[Train/Legends|train]] set inspired by the design of a train found on the planet Umbara. The center of the train set was decorated with a holographic Life Day Tree.<ref name="Stronghold" /> During the Galactic Civil War, [[propaganda token]]s issued out by both the Rebel Alliance and the Galactic Empire could be exchanged for many different types of Life Day goods.<ref name="SWG" /> Commercialization of the holiday was evident during an ''[[Action Tidings]]'' Special Report news broadcast, in which [[Serv-O-Droid, Inc./Legends|Serv-O-Droid, Inc.]] sponsored an advertisement featuring an [[ERL-21 transcribot]], used to transcribe the news footage. The advertisement featured a tagline which enticed viewers with the promise of free [[Restraining bolt/Legends|restraining bolts]], so long as they made an order before Life Day.<ref name="ActionTidings" />

===Music and entertainment===
{{Quote|So unless you want to spend your final moments being shaken to death by the dulcet tones of the Kashyyyk Life Day Choir, I'd reconsider.|Gault Rennow threatening Dretcher|audio=GaultRennowLifeDayChoir.flac|<ref name="KOTFE">{{TORcite|exp=kotfe|chapter=13}}</ref>}}
Dancing was another notable aspect of Life Day. [[Sliced Neural Attunement Amplifier]]s were a type of device available on Life Day which, when used, compelled those in the immediate vicinity to break out in dance. Following the Battle of Yavin, Figrin D'an and the Modal Nodes played a number of different musical pieces during Life Day, including [[Unidentified Life Day song (Swingalong Santa)|three]] [[Unidentified Life Day song (Christmas Green)|types]] of [[Unidentified Life Day song (Here We Come A-Wassailing)|jazzy songs]], and a [[Unidentified Life Day song (whimsical)|more whimsical piece]]. Although these Life Day songs were cheerful or upbeat, the band was also known to play a somewhat [[Unidentified Life Day song (ominous)|ominous-sounding song]] during the holiday, and even a [[Mandalorian/Legends|Mandalorian]] war chant known as ''[[Dha Werda Verda]]''. On the other hand, the band was also known to play a celebratory [[Ewok/Legends|Ewok]] song during the holiday, and "[[Ton'yy Rho's Uglehop]],"<ref name="SWG" /> a song that was once played at the [[Vapor Room]] drinking establishment on [[Cloud City/Legends|Cloud City]].<ref name="ForceUnleashed">''[[Star Wars: The Force Unleashed]]''</ref> "[[Symponik Nabooalla]]," a [[symponik]] composed by the [[Gungan/Legends|Gungan]] female [[Augara Jowil/Legends|Augara Jowil]] in the year [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]],<ref name="DB Augie">{{DB|character|augie|Jowil, Augara "Augie"}}</ref>
Even though Wookiees rejected materialism,<ref name="SOELifeDay" /> they nevertheless came to embrace the exchange of presents as a central ritual and a symbol of love. Chewbacca's family, for instance, was known to receive gifts during the holiday. Chewbacca's son, [[Lumpawaroo/Legends|Lumpawaroo]], accepted from Saun Dann a [[mini-transmitter]], while [[Attichitcuk/Legends|Attichitcuk]], Chewie's father, accepted a sensual [[Hologram/Legends|holographic]] [[cassette]] of [[Mermeia]], a virtual [[Entertainer|performer]]. [[Mind evaporator/Legends|Mind evaporators]],<ref name="SWHS" /> also known as proton chairs,<ref name="SWG" /> were a type of [[virtual reality]] device which could be used as entertainment. In Attichitcuk's case, the proton chair was used to enjoy the cassette given to him by Saun Dann. Entertainment such as this was not an uncommon indulgence during Life Day. Lumpawaroo, or Lumpy as he was also called, treated himself to a tabletop performance of [[holographic tumbler]]s.<ref name="SWHS" /> [[Holo-entertainment table]]s such as these, as well as proton chairs, were readily available as gifts during Life Day. So too were [[pocket-sized aquarium]]s, a type of novelty [[Aquarium/Legends|fish tank]].<ref name="SWG" /> When Imperial [[Trooper/Legends|troops]] raided Chewbacca's home in search of suspected Rebel activity, Lumpy partook in other forms of entertainment, like watching a [[Unidentified Rebel cartoon|Rebel Alliance cartoon]] on the [[Viewscreen/Legends|screen]] of his [[video book]]. While an [[Unidentified Imperial commander (Blockade of Kashyyyk)|Imperial commander]] and [[Unidentified stormtrooper (Blockade of Kashyyyk)|two stormtroopers]], including [[B4711]], searched the house for evidence, Saun Dann encouraged the [[Unidentified Imperial technician|technician]] of the group to take a brief break to watch a [[Holovid/Legends|holovid]] performance of a [[Unidentified Human band|band]] playing a song called "[[Light the Sky on Fire]]."<ref name="SWHS" /> Singing, playing and listening to music such as this was one of Life Day's most important traditions. In fact, Wookiees were known to play tree-drum music on the holiday as far back as 1,500,000 BBY.<ref name="Slugthrowers" /> The [[Kashyyyk Life Day Choir]] was a [[choir]] responsible for singing Life Day music. In [[3630 BBY]], a [[Devaronian/Legends|Devaronian]] named [[Gault Rennow]] threatened to use a [[sonic amplifier]] on [[Dretcher]]'s hideout container, making the tones of the Kashyyyk Life Day Choir so loud, they would shake him to death.<ref name="KOTFE" /> also became associated with the holiday.<ref name="SWG" /> More importantly, Life Day had its emblematic song, known in [[Galactic Basic Standard/Legends|Basic]] as "A Day to Celebrate"<ref name="SWHS" /> (otherwise referred to as the "Tree of Life"),<ref name="Hope" /> which put emphasis on peace, harmony and freedom.<ref name="SWHS" />

===Emphasis on the arts===
Music was not the only form of artistic expression emphasized during Life Day. Many paintings and sculptures were devoted to the holiday. Oraalarri's family, for instance, bestowed a number of paintings to participating celebrants, including ''Life Day Kashyyyk'', ''Life Day Matriarch'', and ''Life Day Patriarch'', which portrayed important aspects of Wookiee culture. Other paintings were packaged as gifts, like ''[[Pilgrimage]]'', which depicted two Wookiee warriors on Kashyyyk directing a Human female of the Rebel Alliance. Two other paintings were packaged in a similar manner, including ''[[Triumph]]'', which depicted a Wookiee silhouette throwing his arms into the air in a triumphant gesture, and ''[[Memories Past]]'', which depicted a profile view of a Wookiee. Many Life Day paintings emphasized the importance of family, and highlighted many of the holiday's customs. One such [[Life Day Painting (Wookiee family)|painting]] depicted a Wookiee family in a warm embrace, while [[Gift Giving Wookiees|another]] depicted two young Wookiees presenting a Life Day orb to one another. Another [[Proud Wookiee|painting]] depicted a porture of a proud looking male Wookiee, while [[Red Robed Wookiee|another]] depicted a Wookiee wearing a red Life Day robe. Some paintings focused on locations important to the Wookiees, like one [[Kashyyyk at Night|painting]] which depicted a tree settlement on Kashyyyk during nighttime. The painting titled ''Ancient Life Day'' depicted an aged Wookiee wearing a hooded, red Life Day robe, whilst holding a [[Staff/Legends|staff]] in one hand, and a Life Day orb in another. The painting ''[[Family Bonds]]'' depicted a family portrait of Chewbacca's family, wearing red Life Day robes, and carrying Life Day orbs in front of a starry backdrop. Four paintings were also commissioned to depict the four great Wookiee values, ''[[Morality]]'', [[Courage (painting)|''Courage'']], [[Compassion (painting)|''Compassion'']], and ''[[Loyalty]]''. Propagandistic elements were evident in at least one [[Life Day 2009 Painting|Life Day painting]], which depicted [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lord of the Sith]] [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader]] crushing a present, while ominously observing a cheerful celebration of Wookiees holding hands around a Life Day Tree. Certain art sculptures were also made as gifts, including a [[Unidentified piece of art (spike)|spike-like sculpture]], a [[Unidentified piece of art (swan)|swan-like sculpture]], and a [[Unidentified piece of art (flame)|flame-like sculpture]]. [[Wookiee Hero Figurine]]s were made as gifts, and [[Wookiee Ceremonial Shield]]s and [[Wookiee Rifle Display]]s of [[X1 carbine]]s could also be displayed as a form of Wookiee Life Day art.<ref name="SWG" />

===Indulging in treats===
{{Quote|Now then&hellip; what's that I smell? Could it be some of those famous Wookiee-ookiees?|Saun Dann|audio=SaunDannOokiees.flac|<ref name="SWHS" />}}
Feasting on meals and consuming treats was an important aspect of Life Day.<ref name="SWHS" /> During the Life Day of 1 ABY,<ref name="Leland" /> Chewbacca's wife, [[Mallatobuck/Legends|Mallatobuck]], prepared a bowl of Wookiee-ookiees,<ref name="SWHS" /> a crunchy Wookiee treat.<ref name="SWG" /> Her son Lumpy attempted to sneak a [[Cookie/Legends|cookie]] before dinner, but Malla caught him, and asked him to take out the day's garbage. Later on, Malla prepared dinner for the night's feast. She turned on a viewscreen to view a [[Instruction cassette|cooking program]] with [[Gormaanda/Legends|Gormaanda]], a four-armed chef. Gormaanda gave instructions on how to prepare [[Bantha rump|Bantha Surprise]],<ref name="SWHS" /> a traditional Life Day dish.<ref name="SWG" /> However, Malla could not keep up with Gormaanda's instructions, and switched off the viewscreen in frustration.<ref name="SWHS" /> The traditional beverage of [[Hoth/Legends|Hoth]] [[Chocolate/Legends|chocolate]] was a type of [[Hot chocolate/Legends|hot chocolate]] made from tauntaun [[Milk/Legends|milk]], and Life Day candy was also popular during the holiday. Saun Dann had ordered several cases of the candy to give to needy children, only for it to be stolen and eaten by the stormtrooper TK-555 on at least two separate ocassions.<ref name="SWG" /> In the absence of traditional cuisine, Wookiee's sometimes had to improvise their meals. For instance, during their imprisonment, Gyylghrard and his fellow Wookiee slaves had to make do with a ration packet containing rehydrated Corellian ryshcate cake.<ref name="Hope" /> Some Life Day food items were displayed as decorations, such as [[Decorative Varactyl Egg Nog]] and [[Decorative Fruitcake]].<ref name="SWG" /> An especially important part of the Life Day celebration consisted of a spiritual passage; by chewing roots of the Orga plant, the Wookiees would journey in spirit form and join the essence of the Tree of Life. According to the legends, that most ancient tree had been the starting point of the Wookiee civilization. Were the Orga roots lacking, the Wookiee elders were entitled to cancel the holiday.<ref name="TKD" />

===Rejection by the dark side===
[[File:LifeDay2009Painting.png|250px|thumb|Despite official condemnation from Emperor Palpatine himself, the Galactic Empire largely allowed Life Day festivities to continue.]]
While the holiday was largely embraced by both the Galactic Republic<ref name="SWTOR" /> and the subsequent Alliance to Restore the Republic,<ref name="SWG" /> the central themes of Life Day oftentimes ran antithetical to the [[Philosopher/Legends|ideals]] of regimes loyal to the [[Sith/Legends|Sith]]. The old Sith Empire, for instance, considered Life Day to be a disgraceful menace of a holiday which encouraged activities unbecoming of an Imperial citizen, such as dancing in inclement weather, singing unpatriotic carols, and engaging in nonviolent physical contact with Wookiees. The Sith Empire similarly disapproved of snowball fights, as their [[Explosive Ordnance Disposal]] unit expressed concerns that some of the snowball bombs were used to conceal small, suspicious packages. As such, citizens were urged to deliver any suspicious parcels to Imperial EOD for processing and disposal. The Sith Empire also disapproved of the Sleigh I speeder design, for far exceeding the guidelines for maximum "cheerful" ornamentation. Imperial EOD furthermore feared that the parcels and other various Life Day paraphernalia strapped to the rear of the vehicle contained explosive devices.<ref name="Grinch" /> The later Galactic Empire was a largely [[Speciesism|xenophobic]] regime which similarly treated Wookiees as second-class citizens, and enslaved them for various [[Imperial Military/Legends|Imperial Military]] projects.<ref name="Phantom">''[[Star Wars: X-Wing Rogue Squadron: The Phantom Affair]]''</ref> Due in part to their enslavement, Wookiees were oftentimes prevented from celebrating the holiday normally.<ref name="SOELifeDay" /> Indeed, the Empire exhibited little respect for the holiday and its customs. During the Life Day of 1 ABY, the Galactic Empire declared martial law and [[Blockade/Legends|blockaded]] Kashyyyk, which further impeded holiday celebrations on the world. They had also dispatched Imperial [[Agent/Legends|agents]] to violently raid Chewbacca's home in search of suspected Rebel activity, going so far as to completely ransack Lumpy's room, and behead his [[stuffed bantha]] toy.<ref name="SWHS" /> Imperial citizens were encouraged to disrupt holiday activities by smashing gift boxes suspected to contain Rebel contraband,<ref name="SWG" /> and even Galactic Emperor Palpatine personally expressed contempt for the holiday.<ref name="Revealed" /> Nevertheless, Life Day had long since become a popular and mainstream holiday,<ref name="SOELifeDay" /> and both the old Sith Empire<ref name="Grinch" /> and later Galactic Empire proved unwilling to supress celebratory activities entirely.<ref name="Celebrate" /> Despite official condemnation of the holiday, the Sith Empire reluctantly allowed the Master of Ceremonies and his fellow revelers to peddle gifts and carry out celebrations aboard the Vaiken Spacedock. They also allowed for the launching of celebratory fireworks, under the condition that the user assumed sole responsibility for any and all scorching damage pursuant to ignition.<ref name="Grinch" /> Likewise, despite Palpatine's displeasure with the holiday,<ref name="Revealed" /> the Galactic Empire largely allowed Life Day festivities to continue. Under the watchful eye of the Empire, [[Queen/Legends|Queen]] Kylantha of Naboo was allowed to accept a Tree of Life and conduct celebrations in Theed.<ref name="Celebrate" /> Similar celebrations were allowed to be carried out peacefully in other cities, like Coronet<ref name="SWG" /> and Kachirho.<ref name="ROTW" /> Aside from the Imperial governments, the Confederacy of Independent Systems also harbored at least some measure of disdain for the holiday, as exemplified by General Grievous' dastardly attempt to steal Life Day gifts destined for the Talz.<ref name="CWAGrievous" />

===Useage of the term for birthdays===
{{Quote|HAPPY LIFE DAY, BOBRINGI MAFUSA. YOU'RE ONE FINE MON CALAMARI|An electronic banner at Bobringi Mafusa's birthday party|<ref name="Galaxy of Fear: The Doomsday Ship">''[[Galaxy of Fear: The Doomsday Ship]]''</ref>}}
The generalized term "lifeday" or "life day" was at times used to refer to one's [[Birthday/Legends|birthday]].<ref name="Leland" /> Such was the case around 11 [[Standard month/Legends|months]] [[Galactic Standard Calendar|ABY]],<ref name="TERC">''[[The Essential Reader's Companion]]''</ref> when the [[Mon Calamari/Legends|Mon Calamari]] [[Bobringi Mafusa]] celebrated his life day aboard the [[Luxury liner/Legends|luxury]] [[Star Cruiser/Legends|star cruiser]] ''[[Star of Empire]]''. During the occasion, he was served special Mon Calamari [[crab-stuffed creampuff]]s.<ref name="Doomsday">''[[Galaxy of Fear: The Doomsday Ship]]''</ref> In [[13 ABY/Legends|13 ABY]],<ref name="TERC" /> [[Wedge Antilles/Legends|Wedge Antilles]] of the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]] told [[Qwi Xux]] to send him "lifeday presents," seemingly referring to his birthday, rather than the Wookiee holiday.<ref name="Adumar">''[[X-Wing: Starfighters of Adumar]]''</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
===Origin and development===
[[File:StarWarsHS.jpg|150px|thumb|Life Day made its debut in 1978 with the airing of ''The Star Wars Holiday Special''.]]
Wookiee Life Day made its first appearance in the television film ''[[The Star Wars Holiday Special]]'',<ref name="SWHS" /> which aired on [[November 17]], [[1978]].<ref name="Boba Fett: Mystery Man">{{GalaxyCite|1|Boba Fett: Mystery Man in Not-So-Shining Armor}}</ref> The main storyline of the film, based on a story by [[George Lucas]],<ref name="Filmfax 69-70">{{SWArchive|url=movies/saga/20081117.html|text=Holiday Special: Script and Directors}}</ref> transpires on the Wookiee home planet of Kashyyyk. Chewbacca and Han Solo visit the planet to celebrate the Wookiee holiday Life Day with his family, which includes his wife Malla, his son Lumpy, and his father Itchy. As Chewbacca and Han are known Rebel agents, they are pursued by the Galactic Empire, who in the process invade Chewbacca's household. The plot is strung together by a series of musical numbers, celebrity appearances, and other variety-show acts, including songs and comedy routines by such [[1970]]s celebrities as [[Jefferson Starship]], [[Diahann Carroll]], [[Art Carney]], [[Harvey Korman]], and [[Bea Arthur]]. The special introduced many of the key Life Day concepts that were later expanded upon in other sources. The exchange of gifts, the preparing of treats and feasts, playing and listening to music, and sharing time with family were all depicted in the television special as being key components of the Wookiee holiday. So too were other aspects, like burning candles ritualistically, carrying Life Day orbs, and having Wookiees don red robes and join into groups to observe the holiday at the Tree of Life.<ref name="SWHS" /> The red Life Day robes worn by the Wookiees at the end of the special were actually an improvised solution to cover up the lack of Wookiee costumes beyond the masks (which were [[Don Post Studios|Don Post]] brand) due to the special by that point going massively over budget.<ref name="Burman">{{WebCite|url=http://www.starwarsholidayspecial.com/text/tom_burman.htm|text=Interview with Tom Burman, Make-Up Effects|author=Skot Kirkwood|date=2005-05-09|work=The Star Wars Holiday Special|archivedate=20060506135459}}</ref>

In [[1979]], the [[Los Angeles Times Syndicate]] distributed a [[Star Wars (comic strip)|''Star Wars'' newspaper comic strip]] written by [[Russ Manning]]. The comic strip, retroactively titled ''[[The Kashyyyk Depths]]'', depicts a story in which Han Solo, Chewbacca, C-3PO, and R2-D2 return to Kashyyyk for another Life Day celebration. The comic strip introduced other aspects of the holiday, such as the importance of Orga root, and the spiritual and historical significance of the Tree of Life.<ref name="TKD" /> Life Day is also featured in ''[[Kessel: Hell in Space]]'', written by [[Cory J. Herndon]] in May [[2003]]. The [[Planet Hoppers]] article, published by [[Wizards of the Coast]], contains a story about a Wookiee named Gyylghrard who attempts to celebrate Life Day whilst in a prison on Kessel.<ref name="Hope" />

===Portrayal in online video games===
====''Star Wars Galaxies''====
[[File:LifeDay-SWG.jpg|thumb|A Life Day event feature from the ''Star Wars Galaxies'' website]]
The holiday has been explored in much greater detail as a recurring celebratory event in a number of [[Roleplaying game|massively multiplayer online role-playing games]], starting with the [[2003]] [[Star Wars video games|video game]] [[Star Wars Galaxies|''Star Wars Galaxies: An Empire Divided'']], developed by [[Sony]] Online Entertainment and published by [[LucasArts]].<ref name="SWG" /> Life Day was first officially recognized as an in-game holiday by the developers of ''Star Wars Galaxies'' in a [[December 19]], 2003 feature titled "Happy Holidays 2003." In this feature, the developers encouraged players to celebrate Life Day during the months of December and early January. For their part, the developers began dropping numerous Wookiee Life Day orbs and robes in the city halls of player cities that were registered on the planetary map. The developers intended for the [[Mayor/Legends|mayors]] of such cities to share the items with their residents. In addition to letting mayors hand out the items, the developers began attending various live events, and handed out orbs to players and merchants to give away or sell. They continued to hand out orbs and robes throughout the months of December and into January, and ensured that the items did not become exceedingly rare. In addition to the orbs and robes,<ref name="Holiday" /> players could also receive three different types of art sculptures.<ref name="SWG" /> The holiday made a return with the release of Publish 11.5 on [[December 14]], [[2004]].<ref name="Publish2004">{{SonyCite|url=players/content.vm?id=64187&resource=publish|text=Publish Archive 2004}}</ref> This time, the celebration centered around a quest in which players could speak to a Wookiee named Kkatamik, visit his family on either Dathomir, Endor, or Yavin 4, and learn more about the holiday's customs. During the celebratory event, players could receive a gift from the Wookiee elder Oraalarri, including a Life Day orb, or one of three new house paintings. Wookiee players also had the option to choose to receive a Life Day robe.<ref name="SWG" />

The event ended on [[January 13]], [[2005]] with the release of Publish 12. On [[December 13]] of that year, Life Day made a return with the release of Publish 26. This time, the developers simply added two gift boxes to the player's inventory. One gift could be opened by the player, while the other had to be shared with a friend.<ref name="Publish2005">{{SonyCite|url=players/content.vm?id=64886&resource=publish|text=Publish Archive 2005}}</ref> Opening the gift box would temporarily spawn a large, festive wroshyr tree to the tune of the "Symponik Nabooalla." Gifts included three new types of paintings, a Wookiee Hero Figurine, a Wookiee [[Rifle/Legends|Rifle]] Display, a Wookiee Ceremonial Shield, and a Miniature Wroshyr Tree.<ref name="SWG" /> On [[December 22]], the developers also added a new a level-up item called "An Energetic Lifeday Orb." This item could be looted from various NPCs and creatures, and used in order to grant the player an additional experience level.<ref name="Publish2005" /> On [[January 4]], [[2006]], the celebrations were concluded as part of Publish 26.6, and the gift boxes and Life Day orbs could no longer be obtained. Life Day was once again brought back as part of Chapter 4.2: "Armed and Ready for Action!" on [[December 8]] of that year.<ref name="Publish2006">{{SonyCite|url=players/content.vm?id=64186&resource=publish|text=Chapter Archive 2006}}</ref> The activities were not unlike the previous year's. Players once again received two gift boxes, one for themselves, the other for a friend, and opening the box spawned a temporary wroshry tree to celebratory music.<ref name="SWG" /> However, different items were included as gifts, including five new paintings, a Life Day Bunting, Life Day Incense Burner, Life Day Wreath, and Miniature Life Day Tree.<ref name="LifeDay2006">{{SonyCite|url=players/content.vm?id=66922&resource=features|text=Life Day 2006}}</ref>

Life Day returned on [[December 12]], [[2007]], albeit with a considerable number of changes. This time, large wroshyr trees were set up in the cities of Theed, Kachirho,<ref name="Celebrate" /> and Coronet.<ref name="Coronet">{{SonyCite|url=players/news_archive.vm?id=67536&month=122007|text=Celebrate Life Day!}}</ref> By interacting with one of the trees, players would receive two gift boxes, one for themselves, and another for a friend, much like during the previous two Life Day events. By opening the gift box intended for oneself, players would receive an ''Ancient Life Day'' painting and a Hanging Life Day Orb. The gift box given to a friend would contain either one of four items, a Kachirho Wall Cornucopia, Life Day Lamp, Life Day Necklace, or Wookiee Home Banner Kit. As an added component of the 2007 Life Day event, Figrin D'an and the Modal Nodes played festive music under the branches of the Trees of Life.<ref name="Celebrate" /> Songs played by the band included three real world cover pieces, including "Christmas Green," "Here We Come A-Wassailing," and "Swingalong Santa."<ref name="TRE">{{GalaxiesAED}} directory tree files and source data</ref> Under the wroshyr trees, players could also interact with Wookiee Life Day vendors to purchase a unique selection of items, including special Holiday Fireworks Packages, Hoth Chocolate, and Wookiee-ookies. Sliced Neural Attunement Amplifiers were also available,<ref name="Celebrate" /> which when used, would force nearby players to begin dancing.<ref name="SWG" /> In preparation for the game's [[2008]] celebrations, some of the developers watched ''The Star Wars Holiday Special'' in its entirety, and drew a great deal of inspiration from it.<ref name="DevDiary">{{SonyCite|url=players/news_archive.vm?id=68149&month=122008|text=Dev Diary – Creating Life Day}}</ref><ref name="Producer">{{SonyForumsCite|url=swg/posts/list.m?topic_id=794179|text=Producer Note: December 4th, 2008}}</ref> The festivities, which were scheduled to run from [[December 16]], 2008 until [[January 12]], [[2009]], saw the addition of new content. However, the developers strived not to remove features seen during previous events. Dearic, Doaba Guerfel, and Wayfar were this time designated as the celebratory cities, and the Art and Programming Departments added snowfall to them to create a more festive theme. Each city was again installed with a large wroshyr tree, beneath which Figrin D'an and his band played<ref name="Revealed" /> the aforementioned real world Christmas songs.<ref name="TRE" /> Players could again interact with the trees to receive two gift boxes, one for themselves, another for a friend.<ref name="Revealed" /> Interacting with the tree would also award players with a badge titled "Celebrant of Life." Possible gift items included a painting titled ''Family Bonds'', as well as a Holo-Entertainment Table, Proton Chair, and Pocket Aquarium,<ref name="SWG" /> which were directly inspired by ''The Star Wars Holiday Special''.<ref name="Producer" />

These same items could also be purchased by Imperial players from a Trandoshan trader NPC named Sstrigge, and by Rebel players from a Wookiee freedom fighter NPC named Oolovv, by spending propaganda tokens, a type of token which could be earned through participation in Life Day minigames.<ref name="SWG" /> For Rebel players, the minigame entailed decorating Life Day Trees around the three participating cities, whereas Imperial players were tasked with smashing presents around the three same cities.<ref name="Revealed" /> The latter was directly inspired by a scene in the ''Holiday Special'' of Imperial troops smashing Lumpy's presents.<ref name="Producer" /> Neutrally-aligned players could choose to participate in either task. Players had the option of whether or not to decorate and destroy competitively or casually. If the casual option was chosen, players were allowed to finish 10 objectives for the day. If competitive, players had 30 minutes to finish as many objectives as they could. A scoreboard of the daily top three competitive players was also implemented.<ref name="Revealed" /> For each tree decorated, or present destroyed, the player would receive 5 propaganda tokens. However, this could be increased to 15 if the player declared themselves [[Special forces/Legends|Special Forces]], therefore opening them up to attack from other players. Additional items which could be purchased with propaganda tokens included a Kowakian Cage, which if placed in a home, would allow for a festively dressed Kowakian monkey-lizard to roam about the room. Tokens could also be used to purchase Kashyyyk Elite Hunter Bandoliers, Life Day Decorated Young Wroshyr Trees, undecorated Young Wroshyr Trees, Life Day Pile of Presents, and Bantha Surprise Recipes. Imperial players could also purchase Blackmail Packages, while Rebel players could purchase Lists of Favors. Using those items would grant the player 50 GCW points.<ref name="SWG" /> Saun Dann was included as a non-player character for the event,<ref name="Revealed" /> and he supplanted the role of the previous year's Wookiee Life Day vendors by selling goods like the Holiday Fireworks Packages, Hoth Chocolate, and Wookiee-ookies (however, the Sliced Neural Attunement Amplifiers were removed).<ref name="SWG" /> Saun Dann would also offer players a special Life Day quest,<ref name="Revealed" /> the plot of which centered around the theft of candy by an overweight stormtrooper named TK-555. By completing the quest, players had the opportunity to receive a STAP-1 speeder as a transactional reward from Watto.<ref name="SWG" />

When Life Day was deactivated as part of Game Update 6 on January 12,<ref name="GameUpdate6">{{SonyCite|url=players/news_archive.vm?id=68180&month=012009|text=''Star Wars'' Galaxies: Game Update 6}}</ref> Saun Dann was removed, but the other quest NPCs remained for a short time longer to allow players more time to complete the quest.<ref name="LifeDayEnds">{{SonyCite|url=players/news_archive.vm?id=68178&month=012009|text=Life Day Ends Monday, January 12, 2009}}</ref> Life Day was again reactivated on [[December 15]], [[2009]]<ref name="Hotfix2009">{{SonyCite|url=players/news_archive.vm?id=68556&month=122009|text=''Star Wars'' Galaxies: Wookiee Life Day &mdash; On Tuesday, December 15th}}</ref> as part of Hotfix 14.8.<ref name="Hotfix148">{{SonyCite|url=players/news_archive.vm?id=68567&month=122009|text=Star Wars Galaxies: Hotfix 14.8 -- On Thursday, December 17th (US) and Friday December 18th (Europe)}}</ref> The 2009 celebrations were virtually identical to 2008's, albeit with some minor changes. For instance, Saun Dann's quest, which was made repeatable, now had dialogue which referenced the fact that his candy had already been stolen before. Upon completing the quest, players also now had the choice of being awarded with either a Decorative Fruitcake, or Decorative Varactyl Egg Nog. Furthermore, instead of the three real world Christmas songs played during the previous two celebrations, Figrin D'an and his band now played four different ''[[Star Wars]]'' songs, including ''Dha Werda Verda'',<ref name="SWG" /> originally composed by [[Jesse Harlin]] as part of the [[Star Wars: Republic Commando (soundtrack)|soundtrack]]<ref name="RepComSound">[[Star Wars: Republic Commando (soundtrack)|''Star Wars: Republic Commando'' soundtrack]]</ref> for the 2005 video game, ''[[Star Wars: Republic Commando]]''.<ref name="RepCom">''[[Star Wars: Republic Commando]]''</ref> The band also played "[[Juno Eclipse's theme]]," and "[[PROXY and the Skyhook]],"<ref name="SWG" /> two songs composed by [[Mark Griskey]] as part of the [[Musical score|soundtrack]] for the 2008 video game ''[[Star Wars: The Force Unleashed]]''.<ref name="ForceUnleashed" /> The band also played "Ton'yy Rho's Uglehop,"<ref name="SWG" /> yet another song originally composed for ''The Force Unleashed'', this time by Jesse Harlin,<ref name="ForceUnleashed" /> and "[[Victory Celebration]],"<ref name="SWG" /> a theme composed by [[John Williams]]<ref name="ROTJSound">[[Star Wars: Episode VI Return of the Jedi (soundtrack)|''Star Wars'': Episode VI ''Return of the Jedi'' soundtrack]]</ref> for the [[The Star Wars Trilogy Special Edition|''Special Edition'']] of [[Star Wars: Episode VI Return of the Jedi|''Star Wars'': Episode VI ''Return of the Jedi'']].<ref name="ROTJ">{{Film|VI}} {{C|Introduced in [[The Star Wars Trilogy Special Edition|''Special Edition'']]}}</ref> Upon logging in for the holiday, players freely received a new decorative item called the Life Day 2009 Ornament. Interacting with the wroshyr tree would also award a new badge, titled "Life Day Reveler." Likewise, the gift boxes from the tree contained new items, including the ''Life Day 2009 Painting'', a Small Hanging Lamp, a Large Hanging Lamp, and a Kashyyykian Fireplace. In addition to the gift box items, Sstrigge and Oolovv offered items that were not seen during previous celebrations, such as Decorative Wookiee-ookies, Decorative Hoth Chocolate, Life Day Jackets, Holiday Jackets, Rustic Fireplaces, Life Day Kowakian Monkey-lizard Costume Instructions, and Holiday [[Multispectrum disguise suite|Holoshrouds]].<ref name="SWG" /> The event concluded on January 12, [[2010]] as part of Hotfix 14.10.<ref name="Hotfix1410">{{SonyCite|url=players/news_archive.vm?id=68582&month=012010|text=Star Wars Galaxies: Hotfix 14.10 -- On Tuesday, January 12th (US)}}</ref>

Life Day was brought back again on December 14, 2010 as part of Game Update 19.<ref name="Publish2010">{{SonyCite|url=players/content.vm?id=66962&resource=publish#gu190|text=Chapter History 2010}}</ref> Again, few changes were made. Interacting with one of the wroshyr trees would award a new badge, titled "Life Day Merrymaker." The gift box opened for onself would give the player two newly introduced items, including a Life Day Ornament of an R2 unit resembling R2-D2, and a Life Day Decoration Device. The Decoration Device allowed players to flag storyteller props as Wookiee Life Day Decorations. This meant that props used for player-made events would remain persistent for the duration of the holiday. Gift boxes given to a friend would contain one four new paintings, including ''Morality'', ''Courage'', ''Compassion'', and ''Loyalty''. As another change, Figrin D'an and the Modal Nodes went back to playing the three real world songs,<ref name="SWG" /> "Christmas Green," "Here We Come A-Wassailing," and "Swingalong Santa."<ref name="TRE" /> New Life Day-themed items were sold by Sstrige and Oolovv, such as Kashyyykian Bars, Kashyyykian Bar Shelves, Kashyyykian Bar Tables, Life Day Tree Storyteller Tokens, and schematics for Figrin D'an's Holiday Jacket.<ref name="SWG" /> The event's conclusion was planned for [[January 11]], [[2011]],<ref name="LifeDayEnd2011">{{SonyCite|url=players/news_archive.vm?id=69027&month=012011|text=Reminder: Wookiee Life Day Ends On January 11th}}</ref> but it was in fact deactivated on [[January 10]]<ref name="Jan10">{{SonyCite|url=players/news_archive.vm?id=69030&month=012011|text=Star Wars Galaxies: Hotfix 19.2 &ndash; Monday, January 10, 2011}}</ref> as part of Hotfix 19.2.<ref name="Hotfix192">{{SonyCite|url=en_US/players/content.vm?page=Current%20update#gu192|text=Current Update}}</ref> The game's ninth and final Life Day celebration was added as part of Game Update 22 on [[November 17]], 2011,<ref name="GameUpdate22">{{SonyCite|url=players/news_archive.vm?id=69228&month=current|text=Star Wars Galaxies Game Update 22 -- Thursday, November 17, 2011}}</ref> again with minimal changes. Interacting with one of the wroshyr trees would award a badge, this time titled "Life Day Celebrant." The gift box opened for onself would again provide the player with a Life Day Ornament of an R2 unit, and a Life Day Decoration Device. Music played by Figrin D'an and the Modal Nodes was switched back to the same four ''Star Wars'' songs that were played back in 2009. The vendors Sstrige and Oolovv sold items that were previously made available during prior Life Day celebrations, including repackaged gift paintings, like ''Family Bonds'' and the ''Life Day 2009 Painting''.<ref name="SWG" /> As an added change, the developers used the final Life Day celebration as an opportunity to dispense with items that were ordinarily made available during other holiday events, such as [[Empire Day/Legends|Empire Day]], [[Remembrance Day]], the Ewok [[Festival of Love]], and the [[Galactic Moon Festival]]. The Imperial vendor Sstrige would sell Empire Day and Love Day items in addition to the Life Day-themed items, while the Rebel vendor Oolovv would do the same, except dispense with Remembrance Day items in lieu of Empire Day items. Saun Dann was also made to sell Galactic Moon Festival items and the remaining Love Day items.<ref name="SWG" /><ref name="GameUpdate22" /> The final Life Day celebration concluded with the game's closure on December 15, 2011.<ref name="SWG" /><ref name="Shutdown">{{SonyCite|url=playerinfo|text=IMPORTANT INFORMATION ABOUT ''STAR WARS'' GALAXIES™}}</ref>

====''Star Wars: Clone Wars Adventures''====
Sony Online Entertainment was also responsible for the production of the [[Star Wars: Clone Wars Adventures (video game)|''Star Wars: Clone Wars Adventures'' video game]], yet another MMORPG which featured Life Day as a special annual event during the months of December and January.<ref name="CWA" /> The first event was introduced by December 13, 2010,<ref name="CWAForce">{{WebCite|url=http://sony.mediaroom.com/2010-12-13-The-Force-is-Now-With-Mac-Players|text=The Force is Now With Mac® Players|date=2010-12-13|work=Sony MediaRoom|archivedate=20200716051301}}</ref> where players were met with the sight of a Jedi Temple decorated with garlands, Life Day orbs, a large Wroshyr tree, and other festive adornments.<ref name="CWA" /> During the [[December 17]] update, Republic Credits could be earned by clicking on "Republic Credit Orbs" which appeared randomly throughout the Jedi Temple.<ref name="CWAOrbUpdate" /> Credits could in turn be spent on various Life Day-themed items, including a Life Day Decorations Pack which contained various garlands, Life Day orbs, and a present box.<ref name="PackI">{{TCWA|set=Life Day Decorations Pack I}}</ref> Nutracker Clone Trooper armor,<ref name="Nutcracker" /> Protocol Droid Life Day Parts,<ref name="Protocol" /> Life Day robes,<ref name="Robes" /> and wampa suits could also be purchased with credits.<ref name="Wampa" /> On the other hand, Station Cash could be spent on a number of other Life Day items, including yet another Life Day Decorations Pack which contained garlands, orbs, present boxes, and a Wroshyr tree.<ref name="PackII">{{TCWA|set=Life Day Decorations Pack II}}</ref> Station Cash could also be spent on Life Day Clone Trooper armor,<ref name="LifeDayClone" /> Astromech Life Day Parts,<ref name="SnowMaker" /> Mouse Droid Life Day Parts,<ref name="Mouse" /> and an astromech droid named 6R-0WL.<ref name="Growl" /> Another astromech droid, named P3-NUT, could be obtained by donating to the Child's Play Charity event during the 2010 festivities.<ref name="Peanut" /> Other content was added for the Life Day festivities, including a Republic Defender mini-game stage titled "Grievous Steals Life Day."<ref name="CWAGrievous" />
