On [[December 2]], 2011,<ref name="CWALifeUpdate">{{SonyForumsCite|url=cw/posts/list.m?topic_id=6291|text=Game Update Summary - December 2, 2011}}</ref> the Life Day event was reintroduced,<ref name="CWABlog" /> and it copied over much of the content from the previous year, except fewer decorations were placed throughout the temple,<ref name="CWALifeUpdate" /> and [[R2-KT/Legends|R2-KT]] replaced P3-NUT as the Child's Play Charity event prize.<ref name="R2KT">{{TCWA|set=R2-KT}}</ref> However, P3-NUT could still be purchased seperately as a Station Cash item.<ref name="Peanut" /> A Festive Obi-Wan Kenobi outfit which resembled the iconic suit worn by Santa Claus could be purchased with credits,<ref name="ObiWan" /> and on [[December 30]], BR-RR was added as another festive astromech droid which could be likewise be purchased by credits.<ref name="Brrr" /> By the 2011 festivities, a special Life Day-themed home was made available to players, called a "Delightful Festival Hideaway,"<ref name="Delightful">{{TCWA|set=Delightful Festival Hideaway}}</ref> and [[Clone cold assault trooper/Legends|Clone Snowtrooper]] armor was made purchaseable through credits.<ref name="CloneSnowtrooper">{{TCWA|set=Clone Snowtrooper}}</ref> The event was concluded on January 13 of the following year.<ref name="CWALifeEnd">{{SonyForumsCite|url=cw/posts/list.m?topic_id=7445|text=Game Update Summary - January 13, 2012}}</ref> The 2012 Life Day event featured previously included content, except snowfall was added outside the Jedi Temple,<ref name="CWA" /> and Festive Tauntauns were added as an obtainable mount.<ref name="Tauntaun" /> The 2013 featured much of the same,<ref name="CWA" /> and because ''Clone Wars Adventures'' was shut down on [[March 31]] of [[2014]],<ref name="CWAClosure">{{WebCite|url=https://www.clonewarsadventures.com/news/detail.action?articleId=1589|text=With Heavy Hearts, We Announce the Sunset of Clone Wars|author=George, Steve|date=2014-01-24|archivedate=20140127193845}}</ref> it served as the game's final Life Day event.<ref name="CWA" />

====''Star Wars: The Old Republic''====
Life Day is also an ongoing annual event in the 2011 MMORPG ''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic]]'', produced and released by [[BioWare]].<ref name="SWTOR" /> The holiday was first acknowledged by the developers in 2012, as part of Game Update 1.6: Ancient Hypergate released on [[December 11]]. As part of this update, certain Life Day-themed items were made available for sale on the Cartel Market, an in-game microtransaction store in which players exchange Cartel Coins for various in-game merchandise. Items available for purchase included Life Day Robes, an adaptive armor set containing Life Day Vestments, Lower Robe, and Boots, to show off the player's Life Day spirit. The Czerka LD-1 Celebrator, Life Day Tinsel Bombs, Life Day Orbs, and Life Day Holo-Trees were also available for a limited time. Players could also purchase a "Life Day Bundle," a pack which included all of the aforementioned items for a discounted price. Despite offering these Life Day-themed items as early as 2012,<ref name="SWTOR12">{{TORweb|url=patchnotes/1.6.0/ancient-hypergate|text=Game Update 1.6: Ancient Hypergate Patch Notes}}</ref> it would not be until the following year that Life Day was included in the game as an actual event. To kick off their first Life Day event, the developers wrote a tongue-in-cheek news article on [[December 16]], 2013, titled "IMPERIAL EDICT GR-1NC4," written from the perspective of a dissaproving Sith Empire which despised the holiday.<ref name="Grinch" /> The next day, as part of Game Update 2.5.1, the Life Day event was activated. During the event, which lasted until [[January 1]],<ref name="SWTOR13">{{TORweb|url=patchnotes/12172013/game-update-2.5.1-patch-notes|text=Game Update 2.5.1 Patch Notes}}</ref> an NPC named the "Master of Ceremonies," accompanied by a group of fellow Life Day Revelers, could be found aboard the respective space stations for both the Republic and Sith Empire factions. The Master of Ceremonies would sell a number of items to players in exchange for credits, including Life Day Tree fireworks, and Life Day Snowball Bombs. The Life Day Snowball Bombs, when thrown at other players and NPCs, would have a 15% chance of awarding the player with "Snow-Covered Parcels." These parcels were used as an additional form of currency during the event, and could be used in part to buy a Cyan Sphere, as well as a Sleigh I speeder from the Master of Ceremonies. Receiving a parcel would also award the player with a "Jolly Parcel Peddler" achievement, and a Legacy Title called "Life Day Celebrant." Collecting 25 parcels would award an achievement titled "Merry Life Day to All," and collecting 100 would award one called "To All A Good Night," and a Legacy Title named "A Special Snowflake." Subsequent Life Day events in ''The Old Republic'' have thus far followed this same general formula, albeit with added items and some additional content.<ref name="SWTOR" />

The 2014 Life Day event, released as part of Game Update 3.0.1 on December 16, and which ran until [[January 6]], introduced new items sold by the Master of Ceremonies. In addition to the previously available items, the Master of Ceremonies would also sell two versions of a Life Day Holo-Tree, including a [[Gold/Legends|gold]] version and a blue-purple version.<ref name="SWTOR14">{{TORweb|url=patchnotes/12162014/game-update-3.0.1-patch-notes|text=Game Update 3.0.1 Patch Notes}}</ref> New Life Day-themed items were added to the Cartel Market, including a revised "Life Day Bundle" which contained a number of different decorative items, such as icicle and globe ceiling lights, a holo-tree, icicle mounds, potted trees, a Life Day Reveler, a snow blower, a wall freezer unit, and a wampa rug. Other newly introduced Cartel Market items included a Hoth Wampa Cub, and the Vectron J0-1Y speeder. For 2014, new content in the form of an additional mini-game was added. Around the Coruscant Senate, the Dromund Kaas City memorial, and Nar Shaddaa promenade, players could find Life Day Droids, which could be used as targets for Snowball Bombs. Hitting Life Day Droids in this manner could award parcels. The droids also had a chance to respawn as a rarer version called a "Overheated Life Day Droid." This droid had a chance to award an achievement titled "Holiday Hero," as well as a chance to drop decorations, including one of four differently colored holo-trees.<ref name="SWTOR" /> The [[2015]] festivities were scheduled as part of Game Update 4.0.3, running from December 15 to [[January 5]].<ref name="SWTOR15">{{TORweb|url=patchnotes/1272015/game-update-4.0.3|text=Game Update 4.0.3}}</ref> Several items which were originally sold on the Cartel Market, such as the Czerka LD-1 Celebrator, Hoth Wampa Cub, Life Day Vestments, Lower Robe, and Boots, Life Day Tinsel Bombs, and Life Day Orbs, were now sold by the Master of Ceremonies in exchange for parcels. In their place, new Life Day items were offered in exchange for Cartel Coins, including an Ambient Machine which generates a snowstorm, Life Day Ceiling Lights, Life Day Fireplaces, Life Day Pedestals, a Snowstorm Assault Speeder, Life Day Snowball Cannons, and Festive Life Day Robes, which spawn a small orb that follows the player around.<ref name="SWTOR" />

The [[2016]] festivities were released as part of Game Update 5.0.1, running from December 13 to January 10.<ref name="SWTOR16">{{TORweb|url=patchnotes/12132016/game-update-5.0.1-patch-notes|text=Game Update 5.0.1 Patch Notes}}</ref> For this year, new items were added to the Cartel Market, including several Droid Ecosamples, a Festive Weapon Tuning ability, a wampa creature companion, a Festive Tauntaun Mount, and Life Day Holo-Shrubs.<ref name="SWTOR" /> The [[2017]] Life Day event was activated as part of Game Update 5.6.1,<ref name="SWTOR17">{{TORweb|url=patchnotes/12122017/game-update-5.6.1|text=Game Update 5.6.1}}</ref> running from December 12 to January 10.<ref name="SWTOR17B">{{TORweb|url=info/in-game-events|text=DECEMBER AND JANUARY IN-GAME EVENTS|oldversion=20171218235254}}</ref> Again, new items were added to the Cartel Market, including a Model Umbaran Train, a Copero Jubilee Miniprobe, Snowtacular flair, a Merry Ice Tromper, and a Life Day Surprise, which allows for players to burst out from inside a gift box.<ref name="SWTOR" /> Life Day was again released in [[2018]] as part of Game Update 5.10: Jedi Under Siege,<ref name="SWTOR18">{{TORweb|url=patchnotes/12112018/game-update-5.10-jedi-under-siege|text=Game Update 5.10: Jedi Under Siege Patch Notes}}</ref> running from December 11 to [[January 15]].<ref name="SWTOR18B">{{TORweb|url=info/in-game-events|text=In-Game Events}}</ref> For this year, most of the content remained unchanged. Some new content was added, however, for the [[2019]] festivities,<ref name="SWTOR" /> released as part of Game Update 6.0.2a,<ref name="SWTOR19">{{TORweb|url=patchnotes/12172019/game-update-6.0.2a|text=Game Update 6.0.2a}}</ref> and running from December 17 to [[January 7]].<ref name="SWTOR19B">{{TORweb|url=info/in-game-events|text=DECEMBER IN-GAME EVENTS|oldversion=20191218101647}}</ref> A number of new Life Day Snowglobes representing various planets were offered on the Cartel Market. More notably, a new repeatable mission titled "Could Use a Good Hug" was added for the event. The mission called for players to embrace a total of ten Wookiee revelers and carolers, completion of which would award the player with two Snow-Covered Parcels.<ref name="SWTOR" />

===Earthly analogue===
Life Day was most likely originally intended to serve as an [[in-universe]] analogue for the American holiday of [[Wikipedia:Thanksgiving|Thanksgiving]],<ref>{{WebCite|url=https://www.empireonline.com/movies/features/star-wars-holiday-special|text=The Star Wars Holiday Special: may the farce be with you|author=William Thomas & Ian Freer|date=2015-12-03|work=[[Wikipedia:Empire (film magazine)|Empire]] #235 (January 2009)|archivedate=20200527174952}}</ref> as ''The Holiday Special'' was originally aired on November 17, the Friday before Thanksgiving that year.<ref name="Boba Fett: Mystery Man" /> However, over time the term "holiday special" has caused many to misinterpret Life Day as a stand-in for [[Wikipedia:Christmas|Christmas]], leading to games like ''Star Wars Galaxies'' and ''[[Star Wars Battlefront: Renegade Squadron]]'' to place Life Day on or around [[December 25]].<ref name="SWG" /><ref name="Battlefront">''[[Star Wars Battlefront: Renegade Squadron]]''</ref> The confusion has reached the point where ''The Star Wars Holiday Special'' has been referred to as the "Christmas special" by a number of individuals, including producer [[Gary Kurtz]].<ref name="Vanity Fair">{{WebCite|url=https://www.vanityfair.com/magazine/2008/12/star_wars_special200812|text=The Han Solo Comedy Hour!|author=DiGiacomo, Frank|date=2008-12-22|work=Vanity Fair|archivedate=20200113025908}}</ref> In ''Star Wars Galaxies'', the developers eschewed real world meta-references to Christmas during the first couple Life Day events, instead focusing solely on elements of Wookiee culture. However, starting in 2005, the developers began to incorporate Christmas-like elements, namely in the form of wroshyr trees which resembled festively decorated [[Wikipedia:Christmas tree|Christmas trees]]. Later Life Day events incorporated even more Christmas elements, including wreaths, present boxes, and Christmas carols played by Figrin D'an and the Modal Nodes.<ref name="SWG" />

Similar Christmas elements were carried over by Sony Online Entertainment to the Life Day events in ''Star Wars: Clone Wars Adventures'', which also included festively decorate wroshyr trees, as well as a number of droids, armor, clothing, and items which mirrored real world Christmas counterparts.<ref name="CWAGeneric">[[Star Wars: Clone Wars Adventures (video game)|''Star Wars: Clone Wars Adventures'']]</ref> For instance, the astromech droid P3-NUT,<ref name="Peanut" /> as well as Nutcracker Clone Trooper armor was a reference to [[Wikipedia:The Nutcracker|''The Nutcracker'']],<ref name="Nutcracker" /> a real world ballet often associated with the Christmas season.<ref name="Fisher">''Nutcracker Nation: How an Old World Ballet Became a Christmas Tradition in the New World''. Yale University Press. {{ISBN|0300105991}}.</ref> ''Clone Wars Adventures'' also featured festive Obi-Wan clothing which resembled the suit worn by [[Wikipedia:Santa Claus|Santa Claus]],<ref name="ObiWan" /> an astromech droid named BR-RR which resembled a [[Wikipedia:Snowman|snowman]],<ref name="Brrr" /> and festive tauntauns which resembled [[Wikipedia:Santa Claus's reindeer|Santa Claus's reindeer]].<ref name="Tauntaun" /> ''Star Wars: The Old Republic'' also incorporates festive tauntauns, specifically a version which resembles [[Wikipedia:Rudolph the Red-Nosed Reindeer|Rudolph the Red-Nosed Reindeer]]. ''The Old Republic'' also features festive Life Day vehicles, including two which resemble Santa's sleigh, including the Sleigh I and J0-1Y specifically. The game's Master of Ceremonies, an NPC responsible for offering gifts, also resembles Santa Claus. Aside from a number of other items which resemble real world Christmas decorations and toys, ''The Old Republic'' also incorporates other elements associated with the Christmas season, such as snowball fights, and other winter themes.<ref name="SWTOR" /> As Christmas is a [[Wikipedia:winter solstice|solstice]] festival,<ref name="Astronomy">''Astronomy Methods: A Physical Approach to Astronomical Observations''. Cambridge University Press. {{ISBN|0521535514}}.</ref> ''Star Wars Galaxies'' and ''Clone Wars Adventures'' also included such elements as snowfall, as a means by which to appeal to the Christmas spirit.<ref name="SWG" /><ref name="CWA" /> All this was done despite the fact that from an in-universe perspective, Life Day originated on Kashyyyk,<ref name="CWABlog" /> a tropical world devoid of such winter-like elements.<ref name="DB" />

On a related note, a ''Star Wars Galaxies'' website feature titled "''Corellia Times'' Exclusive: Life Day Revealed," has Emperor Palpatine saying "Bah, humbug!" with implied disgust for the holiday.<ref name="Revealed" /> This is a reference to [[Wikipedia:Ebenezer Scrooge|Ebenezer Scrooge]] regarding his views on Christmas in the [[Wikipedia:Charles Dickens|Charles Dickens']] book [[Wikipedia:A Christmas Carol|A Christmas Carol]].<ref name="Dickens">''A Christmas Carol''. CreateSpace Independent Publishing Platform. {{ISBN|1503212831}}.</ref> Similarly, the Sith Imperial edict in ''Star Wars: The Old Republic'', GR-1NC4,<ref name="Grinch" /> is an indirect reference to the [[Wikipedia:Grinch|Grinch]] character from [[Wikipedia:Dr. Seuss|Dr. Seuss's]] [[Wikipedia:How the Grinch Stole Christmas!|''How the Grinch Stole Christmas!'']], who also had similar disdain for Christmas to the extent of initially going out of his way to steal it.<ref name="StealChristmas">''How the Grinch Stole Christmas!''. Random House Books for Young Readers. {{ISBN|0394800796}}.</ref> The Grinch was similarly referenced in the ''Star Wars Galaxies Life Day 2009 Painting'', which depicted a group of Wookiees holding hands around a decorated Life Day tree, with Darth Vader ominously looming in the background whilst crushing a present.<ref name="SWG" /> The scene closely resembles a scene from the [[1960s|1966]] television special of [[Wikipedia:How the Grinch Stole Christmas! (TV special)|''How the Grinch Stole Christmas!'']], which shows the Whos of [[Wikipedia:Whoville|Whoville]] gathering around a Christmas tree in song.<ref name="StealChristmasTVShow">{{VisualMediaCite|title=[[Wikipedia:How the Grinch Stole Christmas! (TV special)|''How the Grinch Stole Christmas!'']]|director=[[Wikipedia:Chuck Jones|Chuck Jones]] and [[Wikipedia:Ben Washam|Ben Washam]]|prod=The Cat in the Hat Productions|year=[[1960s#1966|1966]]}}</ref> In the ''Star Wars: Clone Wars Adventures'' video game, the Republic Defender mini-game stage titled "Grievous Steals Life Day" served as yet another obvious reference to the Dr. Suess story. In the mini-game, all of the dialogue spoken by Commander Cody and General Grievous was done in a poetic meter.<ref name="CWAGrievous" />

===Pop culture references===
The infamous ''Holiday Special'',<ref>{{WebCite|url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/life/tv/2018/11/19/remembering-star-wars-holiday-special-1978/2027329002|text=Remembering that infamously bad 'Star Wars' holiday special, 40 years later|author=McKairnes, Jim|date=2018-11-19|work=USA Today|archivedate=20200513101819}}</ref> and by extention Life Day, has received a number of references in pop culture media. Stomptokyo.com created an [[April 1|April Fools']] joke about a sequel to ''The Holiday Special'' specifically designed to be a Christmas special, taking place on the snowy planet Hoth with [[Dooku/Legends|Darth Tyranus]] dressed as Santa Claus.<ref name="Stomptokyo">{{WebCite|url=http://www.stomptokyo.com/movies/v/very-star-wars-xmas.html|text=A Very Star Wars Christmas|date=2002-04-01|archivedate=20200827213805}}</ref> Life Day was mentioned in [[Wikipedia:The Venture Bros.|''The Venture Bros.'']] episode [[W:c:venturebrothers:A Very Venture Christmas|"A Very Venture Christmas"]],<ref name="VentureBros">{{VisualMediaCite|title=[[Wikipedia:The Venture Bros.|''The Venture Bros.'']]|episode=[[W:c:venturebrothers:A Very Venture Christmas|A Very Venture Christmas]]|director=[[Wikipedia:Christopher McCulloch|Jackson Publick]]|prod=NoodleSoup Productions|year=[[2004]]}}</ref> and in issue #121 of [[Wikipedia:ToyFare|''ToyFare'']] magazine, the "Twisted Toyfare Theater" section is devoted exclusively to ''The Star Wars Holiday Special'', with Lumpy questioning Chewbacca about Life Day, and Chewbacca responding that he should look it up on [[Wookieepedia]].<ref name="OfficialBlog-Latest ToyFare Riffs on Holiday Special">{{OfficialBlog|url=2007/07/18/latest-toyfare-riffs-on-holiday-special|text=Latest ToyFare Riffs on Holiday Special}}</ref> Life Day is mentioned in [[Wikipedia:The Big Bang Theory|''The Big Bang Theory'']] episode [[W:c:bigbangtheory:The Proton Transmogrification|"The Proton Transmogrification"]],<ref name="TBS">{{WebCite|url=https://www.tbs.com/shows/the-big-bang-theory/season-7/episode-22/the-proton-transmogrification|text=''The Big Bang Theory'' S7, E22 The Proton Transmogrification|work=[https://www.tbs.com TBS]|archivedate=20200827215200}}</ref> and the ending of the song "Merry Christmas From Cell Block 2" by Matthew Ebel has his robot companion Proto wishing him a "Happy Life Day." This discrepancy was noticed by Ebel and was quickly corrected to "Merry Christmas."<ref name="MatthewEbel">{{WebCite|url=https://store.matthewebel.com/track/merry-christmas-from-cell-block-2|text=Merry Christmas from Cell Block 2|work=The High Orbit Holiday Special|archivedate=20200727021629}}</ref> Near the end of the year&mdash;during the holidays&mdash;[[StarWars.com]] has often wished its readers a happy Life Day.<ref>{{SWArchive|url=community/fun/polls/OriginalAllPolls.html|text=All Previous Polls}}</ref><ref>{{HBCite|74}}</ref>

===Non-canon history===
[[File:MenaceSithLifeDay.png|200px|thumb|A group of Wookiees celebrating Life Day are left anguished after Cad Bane storms into their home.]]
The following details stories that were not deemed [[canon]] within [[Star Wars Legends|''Star Wars'' Legends]] due to their disregard for established continuity.

====LEGO ''Star Wars'' online material====
{{Quote|But Life Day isn't for another two weeks!"<br />"I've got an idea.|1137 and 1139|<ref name="AlwaysCount">{{LEGOWeb|subdomain=starwars|url=en-us/Comics/comic3.aspx|text="Always count your clones before take-off"|int=Always count your clones before take-off|sw_url=video/view/000886.html|nolive=1|nobackup=1}}</ref>}}
''[[Always count your clones before take-off]]'' was the third in a series of comics available on the [[LEGO Star Wars|LEGO ''Star Wars'']] website. The plot of the story follows two clone troopers, [[1137]] and [[1139]], who are left stranded after their fellow clones leave them behind. While stranded, the clone troopers discover a crate containing a [[TX-130 Saber-class fighter tank/Legends|TX-130 ''Saber''-class fighter tank]]. On the side of the crate is a sign reading, "DO NOT OPEN UNTIL LIFE DAY." Even though the holiday was not for another two weeks, the troopers decide to open the crate anyways.<ref name="AlwaysCount" />

====''LEGO Star Wars: The Yoda Chronicles''====
In ''[[Menace of the Sith]]'', the second episode of ''[[LEGO Star Wars: The Yoda Chronicles]]'', the [[Duros/Legends|Duros]] [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunter]] [[Cad Bane/Legends|Cad Bane]] mistakingly storms into a home of Wookiees celebrating Life Day. When the Wookiees growl angrily at Bane and toss a beverage at him, he apologizes and promptly leaves.<ref name="SithMenace">{{YodaChronicles|Menace of the Sith}}</ref>

====''Star Wars: Tiny Death Star''====
In ''[[Star Wars: Tiny Death Star]]'', Life Day is referred to as "L-Day," and citizens celebrate the holiday by consuming [[Ice cream/Legends|ice cream]].<ref name="Tiny">''[[Star Wars: Tiny Death Star]]''</ref>
